questions.question_text: A car leaves home and travels away at a steady $40$ km/h for $1$ hour $30$ minutes. Construct its distance–time graph. Which description gives the complete graph? Coordinates are $(\text{elapsed time in hours},\text{distance from home in km})$.

options.why: Wrote $1$ hour $30$ minutes as $1.3$ hours, then calculated $40\times1.3=52$ km.
Put the final distance at the initial time and drew a stop instead of travel away from home.
Drew a return home instead of the stated journey away from home.

questions.solution_text: The initial point is $(0,0)$. Convert $1$ hour $30$ minutes to $1.5$ hours. Using $d=st$, the distance is $40\times1.5=60$ km. Plot $(1.5,60)$ and join it to $(0,0)$ with a straight line.

questions.question_text: A walker leaves home, walks $3$ km in $1$ hour, rests for $30$ minutes, then walks a further $2$ km away from home in $1$ hour. Each walking stage is at a steady speed. Construct her distance–time graph. Which description gives the complete graph? Coordinates are $(\text{elapsed time in hours},\text{distance from home in km})$; join consecutive points with straight lines.

options.why: Omitted the $0.5$ hour rest and its horizontal segment.
Reset the distance to zero during the rest instead of keeping the walker $3$ km from home.
Used the final stage's $2$ km as the distance from home instead of adding it to the first $3$ km.

questions.solution_text: Plot $(0,0)$ initially and $(1,3)$ after the first walk. The rest ends at $(1.5,3)$. The second walk ends at $(2.5,5)$ because $3+2=5$ km. Join consecutive points; the rest is horizontal.

questions.question_text: A runner leaves home, runs $6$ km away in $30$ minutes, rests for $15$ minutes, then runs straight home in $45$ minutes. Both running stages are at steady speeds. Construct the distance–time graph. Which description gives the complete graph? Coordinates are $(\text{elapsed time in minutes},\text{distance from home in km})$; join consecutive points with straight lines.

options.why: Added the return distance to the vertical reading as though the axis showed total distance travelled.
Omitted the $15$ minute rest and started the return immediately.
Used $30$ minutes for the return instead of the stated $45$ minutes.

questions.solution_text: Plot the initial point $(0,0)$. The outward run ends at $(30,6)$ and the rest ends at $(45,6)$. The runner reaches home after $30+15+45=90$ minutes, giving $(90,0)$. Join consecutive points with straight lines.

questions.question_text: A driver leaves home, travels $20$ km away in $1$ hour, stops for $30$ minutes, then travels a further $30$ km away in $1$ hour $30$ minutes. Both driving stages are at steady speeds. Construct the distance–time graph. Which description gives the complete graph? Coordinates are $(\text{elapsed time in hours},\text{distance from home in km})$; join consecutive points with straight lines.

options.why: Used only the second driving stage's $30$ km instead of the cumulative distance $20+30=50$ km.
Left out the $0.5$ hour stop and its horizontal segment.
Drew a return home even though the final stage travels farther away.

questions.solution_text: Plot $(0,0)$ initially, $(1,20)$ after the first drive and $(1.5,20)$ after the stop. The final time is $1+0.5+1.5=3$ hours and the final distance is $20+30=50$ km. Join consecutive points through $(3,50)$.

options.why: Started the added stage before the half-hour stop ended.
Used the new stage's $90$ km as the final distance from home instead of adding it to $80$ km.
Subtracted the speed value $60$ from $80$ instead of adding the stage distance $60\times1.5=90$ km.

questions.solution_text: The supplied graph ends at $(2,80)$. Using $d=st$, the added stage covers $60\times1.5=90$ km. Its endpoint is $(3.5,170)$ because $2+1.5=3.5$ hours and $80+90=170$ km. Keep the supplied stages and draw a straight line from $(2,80)$ to $(3.5,170)$.

questions.question_text: A driver leaves home and travels away at $72$ km/h for $25$ minutes, stops for $20$ minutes, then continues away at $48$ km/h for $1$ hour $15$ minutes. Both driving stages are at constant speeds. Construct the distance–time graph. Which description gives the complete graph? Coordinates are $(\text{elapsed time in minutes},\text{distance from home in km})$; join consecutive points with straight lines.

options.why: Omitted the $20$ minute stop, giving $25+75=100$ minutes and no horizontal segment.
Used only the second stage's $60$ km as the final distance from home instead of $30+60=90$ km.
Treated $25$ minutes as $0.25$ hours and $1$ hour $15$ minutes as $1.15$ hours, giving $72\times0.25=18$ km and $48\times1.15=55.2$ km.

questions.solution_text: The initial point is $(0,0)$. The first distance is $d=st=72\times\frac{25}{60}=30$ km, giving $(25,30)$. The stop ends at $(45,30)$. The second stage takes $75$ minutes, or $1.25$ hours, and covers $48\times1.25=60$ km. The final point is $(120,90)$ because $25+20+75=120$ minutes and $30+60=90$ km. Join consecutive points with straight lines.
